scope: A replacement of unrevealed Fire Blast by level-one Growl preserves the original egg-move combination and all other roster fields. Both rosters pass the native flat-learnset validator; the archived source learnsets also identify Growl as a level-one move, with no new egg/event constraint. Both complete engine logs, side-one protocol projections and 39 Observer snapshots are identical. The first hidden move is never selected before the target. Original guarded keys are checked at each corpus decision and every recorded chance-path child. Each alternative ledger uses its own guarded identity. Against the Growl roster every pure side-one first action has security zero: Growl then Earthquake defeats Double Edge; Earthquake twice defeats the other three. A half Double Edge / half Earthquake first move followed by Double Edge has a strictly positive guarantee against every opposing first action and adaptive later choices. Mixed-policy weights are fixed before the simultaneous choice. Thus the previous full-state filter can remove all positive-security policies under an observationally identical legal roster. This is a two-roster counterexample to transferring that filter, not a solution of the complete information set or a claim about an optimal Bayesian prior. Partial enumeration and horizon leaves remain [0,1]. Production bot code is unchanged; no human-player calibration is used.
